transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-03
Time: 14:21 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Nina Rao (AlphaFintech Head of Platform), Jared Kim (AlphaFintech ML Eng), Priya Menon (CTO), Abe Torres (SRE), Elena Gomez (Redwood CSM - listening)

Summary:
Weekly POC check-in focusing on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policies. Reviewed preliminary benchmark numbers from last week's run, clarified burst patterns and target SLOs, agreed on additional stress test to validate warm pool and burst credits, and next steps to produce a sizing spreadsheet and schedule a canary.

Topics discussed: capacity planning, autoscaling policy knobs (min/max pool size, cooldowns), burst planning and warm pools, KV cache warming strategy, quantization tradeoffs, monitoring + tracing for 95th latency, fallback to hosted during sustained overload, security/SOC2/KMS questions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45-ish minutes and then stay on if people have follow ups. Quick check on who's here.
[00:08] Nina: Hi, Nina here, obviously i'm our platform lead, and jared from the ML team is here too.
[00:12] Jared: Yup hi, sorry audio is a little low.
[00:15] Sofia: No problem — Marco joining from SE.
[00:18] Marco: Hey all. I'll jump into the sizing notes after we run through the numbers.
[00:23] Priya: Priya here, CTO. I'm mainly listening for risk and cost.
[00:27] Abe: Abe (SRE). we'll want to know autoscale triggers and any cold start impacts.
[00:31] Elena: Elena — CSM — quick note, i'll follow up on the SOC2 packet.

[00:45] Sofia: Okay, recap from last week - we ran the short burst bench on hosted and saw good latencies sub 200ms p50 but p95 spiked when concurrent requests hit the KV cache miss path. Jared, can you explain the traffic shape you sent?
[01:02] Jared: Sure — most requests are short chat messages median token length ~48, but tails are long sometimes up to 220 tokens. We get a steady baseline of ~6 qps per endpoint during business hours with bursts up to 48 qps for 30-90 seconds during product events. The histogram i sent should be in the sheet.
[01:20] Nina: The important bit: sustained qps is small but bursts are frequent twice daily. We care about 95th latency under 300ms for small requests — anything above that impacts UX.
[01:32] Marco: Right — for Dedicated sizing we consider both steady-state throughput and burst headroom. Two handles: min pool for steady and burst pool/warm buffer plus autoscale cooldowns.
[01:40] Sofia: Marco have you taken a pass at a concrete GPU count?
[01:44] Marco: i did a rough calc based on our bench numbers. For the quantized model variant (4-bit) and typical 64 token requests, one h100-like instance can do roughly 180 tokens/sec at p50 with batching, which translates to about 2.2 qps for 64-token requests? (voice overlap) sorry math — bottom line we estimate need for steady 6 qps per endpoint -> about a 0.5 of a GPU per endpoint; overall for their 12 endpoints i'd recommend starting with a 6-GPU Dedicated pool with a 2-GPU warm burst buffer.
[02:15] Priya: Wait 6 GPUs seems high, can you show cost tradeoffs vs running hosted with autoscale?
[02:20] Sofia: we did compare — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token after commit, hosted is cheaper for small usage but cost spikes for predictable bursty traffic and you can hit throttles. We'll send a cost model.
[02:28] Jared: I want to call out KV cache: most p95 spikes happen when KV cache cold misses happen on longer tails. Can we preload common prefixes?
[02:36] Marco: Yes, we recommend a small preloader job that warms KV cache for top N user prefixes before planned events. Also prefix caching + continuous batching helps. For unexpected bursts the warm buffer reduces cold starts.
[02:46] Abe: How does autoscale trigger — by gpu util, queue length, or token backlog? We need to know cause/effect and cooldowns.
[02:54] Marco: Our autoscaler supports multiple signals — gpu utilization, request queue length, and a token-based backlog metric. Best practice: set min pool to handle steady qps, set scale-up trigger at 70% GPU util, scale-down cooldown of 3-5 minutes to avoid oscillation, and enable burst policy which allows use of reserved burst capacity for short spikes.
[03:12] Nina: How fast can we spin up new bound GPUs on Dedicated?
[03:16] Marco: Warm buffer is key — cold allocations take minutes if provisioning new hardware; but within a Dedicated pool, scaling between nodes is usually sub-60 seconds for adding containers to warm GPUs. If you need sub-5s responses to spikes you must keep a warm reserve or use hosted fallback.
[03:28] Priya: Ok that suggests we'll need a warm reserve. What's the recommended warm buffer size as a percentage?
[03:33] Marco: For their burst shape, i'd say 25-35% of expected peak. So if peak is 48 qps, and steady is 6 qps, warm buffer to cover ~12 qps — that's the 2 GPUs i suggested.
[03:45] Sofia: i'll note that we can also do a hybrid policy: fallback to hosted for overflow up to a rate limit, to avoid paying for big Dedicated pools for rare peaks.
[03:53] Jared: That hybrid fallback is interesting — but we need to ensure data residency + no telemetry leaves VPC for some endpoints.
[03:59] Nina: Right — some endpoints are regulated, so fallback must be opt-out per route. Can the routing policy be per-route?
[04:05] Marco: yes, we support per-route routing rules; you can pin high-sensitivity endpoints to Dedicated only. Fallback can be enabled only for routes that are not regulated.
[04:14] Elena: (typing) i'll include routing rules doc link in follow up.

[04:25] [Bench recap]
[04:25] Sofia: Marco, quick summary of this morning's bench run on your side — you ran a 5m sustained test with 30s bursts?
[04:30] Marco: Yes. Results: steady p50 120ms, p95 260ms on Dedicated baseline (4 GPUs), with bursts to 45 qps causing p95 to jump to 520ms when KV cold path hit. With a warm buffer of 2 GPUs p95 during bursts stayed ~300-340ms. We also tested quantized 4-bit which improved throughput by ~1.8x but increased variance on long sequences.
[04:55] Priya: So quantization gives cost wins but could risk quality on long tails?
[05:00] Jared: We saw minor hallucination rate increase in long sequences when aggressive quantization used. Need eval set to decide.
[05:06] Marco: Correct. Another lever is dynamic model routing — use full-precision for long requests, quantized for short ones. That reduces cost while keeping tail quality.

[05:20] Abe: On monitoring — will we get token-level tracing so we can correlate p95 spikes to KV misses?
[05:26] Marco: Yes. The Console gives per-request trace ids, token-level latencies, and taggable spans. We can export traces to your observability stack — Jaeger/Datadog.
[05:33] Nina: Good. And audit logs for Dedicated? We need retention of 1 year.
[05:37] Sofia: We offer audit logs integrated with customer KMS and retention options as an add-on; SOC2 docs cover controls.

[05:45] [Policy knobs and canary plan]
[05:45] Marco: For the autoscale policy i propose: min_pool 4 GPUs, max_pool 8 GPUs, warm_buffer 2 GPUs, scale_up threshold 70% util OR 10 req queue depth, scale_down cooldown 300s, burst_allowance 120s. Canary: roll autoscaler changes to 10% traffic, monitor p95 for 30m, then expand.
[06:07] Priya: That min 4 seems less than earlier 6 — why difference?
[06:12] Marco: earlier suggestion assumed 12 endpoints starting full tilt. After looking at their real endpoint mix and median token lengths, consolidated multiplexing gives you more efficiency; 4 GPUs plus warm buffer is our cost-optimal starting point. Spreadsheet will show both 4+2 and 6+2 scenarios.

[06:28] Jared: For the warm buffer, can we preload top 1k prefixes overnight? We have a list.
[06:33] Marco: Yes — preloader can accept a prefix list. We recommend incremental warming 10 minutes before expected events.
[06:40] Abe: if warm buffer is used often will that increase costs? we need to model hourly burn.
[06:44] Sofia: Yes you pay for reserved GPUs while they are warm — that's why hybrid fallback is attractive. We'll show per-hour cost impact in the sizing sheet.

[06:54] [Clarifications and misc mis-transcriptions]
[06:54] Samir: (muffled) question on encryption — do you support HSM?
[06:58] Sofia: We integrate with customer KMS and have HSM options for Private deployments; Dedicated can be integrated with customer KMS in the VPC.
[07:05] Priya: Also legal wants to know about data deletion window.
[07:08] Elena: i'll attach retention policy doc.

[07:15] [Recap and explicit next steps]
[07:15] Sofia: Quick recap — Marco to produce the Dedicated sizing calc + spreadsheet with two scenarios (4+2 warm and 6+2) and a cost comparison to hosted by EOD 2026-02-05. Marco will also run the 10-minute sustained + burst bench and upload logs by 2026-02-06.
[07:33] Marco: I'll also include a canary playbook and suggested metrics to watch (p95, 5xx rate, queue depth, GPU util).
[07:40] Nina: AlphaFintech will provide the traffic histogram and list of regulated endpoints by 2026-02-05.
[07:45] Jared: i'll attach the eval prompt set for long-tail quality checks.
[07:49] Sofia: we'll share SOC2 + KMS notes and Dedicated pricing tiers by 2026-02-05.

[07:55] Priya: Good. For canary gating — what are the stop criteria?
[07:59] Marco: Stop if p95 increases >20% vs baseline, error rate >0.5% or GPU queue depth exceeds safety threshold for >5m.
[08:09] Abe: ok sounds reasonable.

[08:12] Sofia: Any final q's?
[08:15] Priya: None, thanks.
[08:17] Nina: No more here — thanks everyone.
[08:20] Sofia: Great, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and bench results.
[08:24] (meeting ends)
